comparison: Both strongly support the BPIA method development and validation (C3, C34-C35, C37, C52-C63). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment while peer reviewers explicitly endorse it as 'an advance' with 'significantly improved efficiency and signal-to-noise ratio.' Peer result also includes C38 (sensitivity speculation) which OpenEval addresses separately in R12.

Both support the discovery of new Beat-Side interactions (C4, C64). Peer reviewers describe findings as 'successfully and convincingly' identifying novel interactions. OpenEval also addresses phylogenetic mirroring (C65-C66) which peer reviewers accept separately in R6. Peer R2 also includes C73 which OpenEval groups with validation data in R4.

Both support SPR affinity measurements (C5, C67-C72). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of KD values and kinetics. Peer reviewers endorse this as part of 'convincing' biochemical characterization. Peer result also includes C74 which OpenEval addresses in R4 with other validation data.

Both support cell-based validation experiments (C75-C77). OpenEval emphasizes complementary nature of multiple assays. Peer reviewers accept these as part of convincing biochemical data. Peer result focuses on subset of claims while OpenEval R4 also includes C73-C74 from other assays.

Both support phylogenetic analysis findings (C39-C51). OpenEval notes some low bootstrap support indicating uncertainty in duplication order. Peer reviewers accept phylogenetic work without concerns as part of descriptive characterization supporting biochemical findings.

Both support the phylogenetic mirroring inference (C65-C66). OpenEval groups this with new interaction discovery in R2. Peer reviewers accept this as unchallenged descriptive analysis. This represents overlapping coverage of claims between different result groupings.

Both support Side expression pattern data (C6-C8, C83-C100). OpenEval notes C101 is speculative about function. Peer reviewers describe work as 'mostly descriptive' with presentation concerns but accept validity. Peer result also includes C103 which OpenEval addresses in R7 regarding functional redundancy.

Both support Beat-V expression patterns (C9-C10, C104-C113). OpenEval emphasizes complementarity with binding data and functional specialization. Peer reviewers accept descriptive findings as valid though note presentation could be more accessible.

Both rate functional/genetic analysis as uncertain or weak (C102, C115-C117, C120). OpenEval finds evidence 'supported' but notes low penetrance and speculation. Peer reviewers explicitly state manuscript 'ended on a relatively weaker note' and request additional validation including genetic rescue experiments.

Both address CNS synapse formation speculation (C121-C132). OpenEval rates as 'uncertain' noting lack of direct experimental evidence in manuscript. Peer reviewers accept these appropriately-framed speculations based on prior published expression data without challenge.

Both support BPIA sensitivity claims (C36-C38). OpenEval addresses these as logical inferences in separate result R12. Peer reviewers include C38 in their endorsement of the BPIA method as having improved signal-to-noise ratio.

OpenEval R10 addresses background claims from prior work (C1-C2, C19-C33) establishing context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as reviewers focused on novel contributions rather than background summaries.

OpenEval R11 addresses established CSSP knowledge (C11-C18) providing methodological justification. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as reviewers did not separately assess background literature claims.

OpenEval R13 addresses prior Side expression dynamics knowledge (C78-C82) from literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than cited background.
